_comment: Three sections, deliberately kept separate rather than merged into one flat slot list: (1) program_slots and (2) program_finding_slots are the RegulatoryContext vocabulary consumed by engine/regulatory_context.js and engine/applicability.js (the new Applicability Engine). (3) retrieval_slots is the pre-existing Option A/B query-scope routing vocabulary (engine/text_utils.js extractQueryScope target_molecule/target_assay/target_topic) — table-ified here so its Korean/English keyword chain lives in data instead of code, but it is NOT part of the RegulatoryContext design and is not consumed by applicability.js. Keeping them separate avoids conflating 'what retrieval should this query route to' with 'what does the user's program actually look like' — two different questions answered by two different engines.

program_slots.description: Broad molecular modality class of the investigational product.

value_labels.biotechnology: the product is a biotechnology-derived product (e.g. a biologic, monoclonal antibody, or recombinant protein)
value_labels.small_molecule: the product is a small molecule (chemically synthesized) drug
value_labels.atmp: the product is an advanced therapy medicinal product (ATMP), such as a cell or gene therapy

program_slots.description: Specific product format, relevant to which S6(R1)/FDA ADA conditions can bind.

value_labels.monoclonal_antibody: the product is a monoclonal antibody
value_labels.bispecific_antibody: the product is a bispecific antibody or other multi-domain antibody product
value_labels.adc: the product is an antibody-drug/toxin conjugate
value_labels.fusion_protein: the product is a fusion protein
value_labels.therapeutic_protein: the product is a therapeutic protein
value_labels.other: the product is some other modality

program_slots.description: Development stage of the program at the time applicability is being assessed.

value_labels.nonclinical: the program is at the nonclinical stage
value_labels.fih_early_clinical: the program is in first-in-human or early clinical development
value_labels.later_clinical: the program is in later-stage clinical development

program_slots.description: Not present anywhere else in the codebase or schema; introduced for this Applicability Engine spike only.

value_labels.other: the product is administered by another route

program_slots.description: Issuing authority the program needs applicability findings for.
Which regulatory question area the user is asking about. Open-ended; extend as new spike slices are added.

value_labels.ada_assay_validation: this concerns anti-drug antibody (ADA) assay validation
value_labels.stability: this concerns sample or product stability

program_finding_slots.description: Whether, and how many, pharmacologically relevant species exist for the clinical candidate.

value_labels.two_rodent_and_nonrodent: there are two pharmacologically relevant species for the clinical candidate, one rodent and one non-rodent
value_labels.one: only one pharmacologically relevant species is available or identified
value_labels.none: no relevant species exists for the clinical candidate

program_finding_slots.description: Whether the pharmacological target is foreign to the host (e.g. bacterial/viral) or an endogenous ortholog.

value_labels.foreign: the pharmacological target is foreign to the host (e.g. bacterial or viral)
value_labels.endogenous_ortholog: the pharmacological target is an endogenous ortholog

program_finding_slots.description: Whether a tissue cross-reactivity (TCR) study with a human tissue panel is technically feasible for this candidate.

value_labels.yes: a tissue cross-reactivity (TCR) study with a human tissue panel is technically feasible for this candidate
value_labels.no: a tissue cross-reactivity (TCR) study is not technically feasible for this candidate (e.g. it is not a good immunohistochemistry reagent)

no: tcr study might not be technically feasible

program_finding_slots.description: For an antibody-drug/toxin conjugate, whether the conjugated toxin/toxicant is novel or an established one with a sufficient prior safety record.

value_labels.established: the conjugated toxin/toxicant is not novel and there is a sufficient body of prior scientific information about it

program_finding_slots.description: Whether the first-in-human/early clinical trial dosing question concerns healthy volunteers or patients (EMA FIH §7.2 vs §7.3).

value_labels.healthy_volunteer: the trial subjects are healthy volunteers

program_finding_slots.description: Ontology v0.2 (docs/milestone_log.md M6 'Context ontology v0.2'). Whether the patient population has a severe or life-limiting disease (e.g. advanced cancer, oncology) as opposed to a general/typical patient population. Only meaningful when subject_population=patient — it refines that axis, it does not replace it. Promoted from a binding semantic audit: 3 separate EMA FIH §7.3 Conditions (cond.7_3.006, cond.7_3.007, cond.7_3.011) all state this same distinguishing fact, and one (cond.7_3.006) was previously misclassified non_bindable/narrative_reference because the extraction anchored on a citation footnote ('see ICH S9') instead of the actual population-description text — an evidence_span mistake, not a genuine hedge, exposed once this slot existed to bind it to.

value_labels.general: the patient population does not have a severe or life-limiting disease
value_labels.severe_or_life_limiting: the patients have advanced cancer or another severe or life-limiting disease

program_finding_slots.description: Which tier of the FDA ADA multi-tiered testing approach the question concerns.

value_labels.screening: this concerns the screening assay tier
value_labels.confirmatory: this concerns the confirmatory assay tier
value_labels.titration: this concerns the titration assay tier
value_labels.neutralization: this concerns the neutralization assay tier

retrieval_slots._comment: The 'stability' value is query-side-only by design today: no document_scope_profiles.json topic_rule currently produces topic_scope='stability' on any record, because M10's whole-blood stability content (§3.2.8) is not yet structured (docs/product_roadmap.md M3 backlog; test/fixtures/eval_questions.json q8_refusal). Kept here (not deleted) because it is a real recurring query pattern; it will start matching records once that backlog content is extracted. It is documented here explicitly so it is a known, tracked gap rather than a silent one.
